title: Sharks Beat Blues in Overtime to Rekindle Hopes
seoTitle: Sharks Beat Blues in Overtime to Rekindle Hopes
subtitle: Darnell Nurse scores game-winner off Ivar Stenberg assist
excerpt: In a thrilling matchup, the San Jose Sharks beat the St. Louis Blues in overtime, with Darnell Nurse scoring the game-winner off an Ivar Stenberg pass.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On Thursday night, the San Jose Sharks defeated the St. Louis Blues 3-2 in overtime at Enterprise Center in St. Louis. The game-deciding goal was scored by Darnell Nurse at 1:03 of overtime, following a pass from Ivar Stenberg.

How the Game Unfolded

The Blues opened the scoring just 3:52 into the first period, with Connor McMichael capitalizing on a pass from Mason McTavish. The equalizer came at 8:48 of the second period when Tyler Toffoli converted a rebound. In the third, Dillon Dube scored shorthanded, putting the Blues back in front.

Sharks' Comeback

The Sharks responded with a goal from Collin Graf at 6:05 of the third period, leveling the score. The play of Alex Nedeljkovic, in his first start of the season, proved decisive as he made 24 saves to keep the team in contention.

Decisive Overtime Moment

Ivar Stenberg gathered the puck in the defensive circle, pushed forward, and delivered a pinpoint pass to Darnell Nurse, who finished into the left corner near the post. The goal sealed the contest and secured the three points for the San Jose squad.

Key Player Performances

  • Darnell Nurse – game-winning goal, his first with the team since the trade with the Edmonton Oilers.
  • Tyler Toffoli – scored and added an assist, contributing on two scoring plays.
  • Collin Graf – game-tying goal, rounding out the Sharks' offensive line.
  • Alex Nedeljkovic – 24 saves in his season debut.

Impact of Macklin Celebrini's Absence

Captain Macklin Celebrini did not dress due to a lower-body injury, marking the second straight game without the player. Historically, the Sharks hold a 4-10-1 record when Celebrini is out.

Team Reactions

Following the game, head coach Ryan Warsofsky praised the team's resilience and highlighted the importance of Kiefer Sherwood's defensive stop, blocking a shot in the dying seconds of the third period to push the game into overtime. In the locker room, players highlighted the leadership of veterans such as Stenberg and the energy of youngsters like Sam Dickinson, who described "feeling" the game.
